raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Cosmos3 V2V currently loads the full source video through ImageIO and preprocesses conditioning frames on the CPU. This PR adds targeted ACCV-Lab decoding and GPU preprocessing to reduce that overhead.

## Modifications


- Add `SGLANG_USE_COSMOS3_ACCVLAB_GPU_PREPROCESS`, disabled by default.
- Reuse the ACCV-Lab reader and request the conditioning source frames, supporting first/last selection and short-video padding.
- Consume each decoded GPU RGB buffer directly. Decoding and preprocessing remain separate functions; synchronize after processing each frame before the SDK reuses its buffer.
- Add a two-pass Triton Lanczos operator that combines resize, center crop, normalization and HWC-to-CHW conversion while matching Pillow rounding.
- Process each source frame once, then reuse the processed last frame for temporal padding.

Install the optional [ACCV-Lab video decoder](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ACCV-Lab/tree/main/packages/on_demand_video_decoder) and enable:

```bash
export SGLANG_USE_COSMOS3_ACCVLAB_GPU_PREPROCESS=1
```

## Accuracy Tests

- Passed 140 Cosmos3 unit tests, CUDA kernel tests covering 36 geometry/pattern combinations, and 9 actual-video preprocessing cases.
- GPU preprocessing matches CPU/PIL exactly for the same decoded input. The decoder-only and full GPU variants produced byte-identical videos across all 8 requests.
- ACCV-Lab and ImageIO have decoder differences; generated output PSNR against ImageIO was 29.65 dB.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Environment:** one H200 NVL, Intel Xeon Gold 6444Y; Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.7.1. Profiling used Nsight Systems.

**Workload:** Cosmos3-Edge, official `robot_pouring.mp4` (93 frames, 1280×704). Condition on the first 5 frames; generate 45 frames at 832×480, 24 FPS, 35 steps, CFG 5, seed 42.

All offload is disabled. Each variant runs in a separate process with **1 complete warmup + 3 measured requests**, using the default conditioning cache. Guardrails are disabled. Speedups are relative to the **unoptimized ImageIO/PIL baseline**; times are means.

| Version | Video decode/load (ms) | Load speedup | Preprocess (ms) | End-to-end (s) | E2E speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ImageIO + CPU/PIL | 378.154 | 1.000× | 940.626 | 4.410 | 1.000× |
| ACCV-Lab decode only + CPU/PIL | 11.801 | **32.045×** | 566.893 | 4.028 | **1.095×** |
| ACCV-Lab + GPU preprocessing | 7.638 | **49.509×** | 8.480 | 3.457 | **1.275×** |

The decoder-only row is an experimental ablation that retains CPU/PIL preprocessing. Its loading time includes GPU-to-CPU/PIL conversion; the full GPU path keeps frames on GPU. ImageIO loads all 93 frames before selecting the conditioning frames, while ACCV-Lab requests the 5 target frames.

Preprocess timing includes actual GPU completion and padding. End-to-end timing includes MP4 saving. The full GPU path eliminates preprocessing D2H transfers. All three runs recorded zero thermal-slowdown increments.

### GPU memory overhead

Same workload and 1-warmup/3-request protocol; values are MiB. PyTorch peaks use exact allocator counters; total device memory includes ACCV-Lab allocations and is sampled through NVML with a 5 ms target interval.

| Metric | ImageIO baseline | GPU preprocessing | Increase |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PyTorch allocated peak | 10768.9 | 11179.3 | +410.4 |
| PyTorch reserved peak | 12152.0 | 12358.0 | +206.0 |
| Total device peak (NVML) | 14506.9 | 14768.3 | +261.4 |

Total device peak increases by **261.4 MiB (1.8%)**: 206 MiB more PyTorch reserved memory plus approximately 55.4 MiB for ACCV-Lab. Each 45-frame float32 conditioning tensor occupies 205.66 MiB; weak-reference tracking confirmed that previous and current request tensors coexist, explaining the larger active-allocation peak.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""GPU RGB Lanczos resize, center crop and normalization with Pillow rounding."""
+
+import math
+from functools import lru_cache
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+def _sinc(value: float) -> float:
+    if value == 0.0:
+        return 1.0
+    angle = value * math.pi
+    return math.sin(angle) / angle
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
+def _coefficients(source: int, target: int, device: torch.device):
+    """Pillow's RGB resampling uses normalized signed 22-bit coefficients."""
+    scale = source / target
+    filter_scale = max(scale, 1.0)
+    support = 3.0 * filter_scale
+    inv_filter_scale = 1.0 / filter_scale
+    taps = math.ceil(support) * 2 + 1
+    coefficients = np.zeros((target, taps), dtype=np.int32)
+    bounds = np.zeros((target, 2), dtype=np.int32)
+    for out in range(target):
+        center = (out + 0.5) * scale
+        begin = max(int(center - support + 0.5), 0)
+        end = min(int(center + support + 0.5), source)
+        weights = []
+        for pos in range(begin, end):
+            distance = (pos - center + 0.5) * inv_filter_scale
+            weights.append(
+                _sinc(distance) * _sinc(distance / 3.0)
+                if -3.0 <= distance < 3.0
+                else 0.0
+            )
+        # Keep sequential double accumulation, including on Python versions
+        # whose sum() uses compensated summation.
+        total = 0.0
+        for weight in weights:
+            total += weight
+        coefficients[out, : len(weights)] = [
+            int(w / total * (1 << 22) + (0.5 if w >= 0.0 else -0.5)) for w in weights
+        ]
+        bounds[out] = (begin, len(weights))
+    return (
+        torch.from_numpy(coefficients).to(device),
+        torch.from_numpy(bounds).to(device),
+        taps,
+    )
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=8)
+def _normalization(device: torch.device):
+    # Use the same float32 values as NumPy's existing pixel conversion. A table
+    # avoids changing rounding through fused multiply-add or approximate divide.
+    values = np.arange(256, dtype=np.float32) / 127.5 - 1.0
+    return torch.from_numpy(values).to(device)
+
+
+@triton.jit(
+    do_not_specialize=[
+        "source_height",
+        "crop_left",
+        "stride_y",
+        "stride_x",
+        "stride_channel",
+        "taps",
+    ]
+)
+def _horizontal_lanczos(
+    src,
+    dst,
+    coefficients,
+    bounds,
+    source_height,
+    crop_width: tl.constexpr,
+    crop_left,
+    stride_y,
+    stride_x,
+    stride_channel,
+    taps,
+    block: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    index = tl.program_id(0) * block + tl.arange(0, block)
+    valid = index < source_height * crop_width * 3
+    channel = index % 3
+    x = index // 3 % crop_width + crop_left
+    y = index // (3 * crop_width)
+    first = tl.load(bounds + x * 2, valid, 0)
+    count = tl.load(bounds + x * 2 + 1, valid, 0)
+    total = tl.full((block,), 1 << 21, tl.int32)
+    for tap in range(taps):
+        weight = tl.load(coefficients + x * taps + tap, valid, 0)
+        value = tl.load(
+            src + y * stride_y + (first + tap) * stride_x + channel * stride_channel,
+            valid & (tap < count),
+            0,
+        ).to(tl.int32)
+        total += value * weight
+    pixel = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(total >> 22, 0), 255).to(tl.uint8)
+    tl.store(dst + index, pixel, valid)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["crop_top", "taps"])
+def _vertical_lanczos_crop_normalize(
+    src,
+    dst,
+    coefficients,
+    bounds,
+    normalization,
+    crop_height: tl.constexpr,
+    crop_width: tl.constexpr,
+    crop_top,
+    taps,
+    block: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    index = tl.program_id(0) * block + tl.arange(0, block)
+    valid = index < crop_height * crop_width * 3
+    channel = index // (crop_height * crop_width)
+    y = index // crop_width % crop_height + crop_top
+    x = index % crop_width
+    first = tl.load(bounds + y * 2, valid, 0)
+    count = tl.load(bounds + y * 2 + 1, valid, 0)
+    total = tl.full((block,), 1 << 21, tl.int32)
+    for tap in range(taps):
+        weight = tl.load(coefficients + y * taps + tap, valid, 0)
+        value = tl.load(
+            src + ((first + tap) * crop_width + x) * 3 + channel,
+            valid & (tap < count),
+            0,
+        ).to(tl.int32)
+        total += value * weight
+    pixel = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(total >> 22, 0), 255)
+    value = tl.load(normalization + pixel)
+    tl.store(dst + index, value, valid)
+
+
+def resize_crop_normalize_rgb(
+    image: torch.Tensor, height: int, width: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Resize CUDA uint8 HWC RGB to contiguous float32 CHW in [-1, 1].
+
+    Uses aspect-preserving Lanczos resize followed by a center crop, matching
+    Pillow's two-pass uint8 rounding. The input may have a padded row stride.
+    The returned tensor owns its storage, while the input is borrowed only by
+    the horizontal pass. Operations run on the current PyTorch CUDA stream.
+    """
+    if not image.is_cuda or torch.version.hip is not None:
+        raise ValueError("Lanczos RGB preprocessing requires a CUDA tensor")
+    if image.dtype != torch.uint8 or image.ndim != 3 or image.shape[2] != 3:
+        raise ValueError("Lanczos RGB input must be uint8 with shape [H, W, 3]")
+    if height <= 0 or width <= 0 or image.shape[0] <= 0 or image.shape[1] <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("Lanczos RGB input and output dimensions must be positive")
+
+    source_h, source_w = image.shape[:2]
+    scale = max(width / source_w, height / source_h)
+    resized_h = math.ceil(scale * source_h)
+    resized_w = math.ceil(scale * source_w)
+    top = (resized_h - height) // 2
+    left = (resized_w - width) // 2
+    coeff_x, bounds_x, taps_x = _coefficients(source_w, resized_w, image.device)
+    coeff_y, bounds_y, taps_y = _coefficients(source_h, resized_h, image.device)
+    intermediate = torch.empty(
+        (source_h, width, 3), dtype=torch.uint8, device=image.device
+    )
+    output = torch.empty((3, height, width), dtype=torch.float32, device=image.device)
+    _horizontal_lanczos[(triton.cdiv(source_h * width * 3, 256),)](
+        image,
+        intermediate,
+        coeff_x,
+        bounds_x,
+        source_h,
+        width,
+        left,
+        *image.stride(),
+        taps_x,
+        256,
+    )
+    _vertical_lanczos_crop_normalize[(triton.cdiv(height * width * 3, 256),)](
+        intermediate,
+        output,
+        coeff_y,
+        bounds_y,
+        _normalization(image.device),
+        height,
+        width,
+        top,
+        taps_y,
+        256,
+    )
+    return output

+def _get_video_total_frames(video_path: str) -> int:
+    """Read the source video frame count using FFmpeg RAW mode."""
+    import cv2
+
+    # RAW mode skips normal decoder initialization.
+    capture = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path, cv2.CAP_FFMPEG, [cv2.CAP_PROP_FORMAT, -1])
+    try:
+        if not capture.isOpened():
+            raise ValueError(f"Cannot open source video: {video_path!r}")
+        total_frames = int(capture.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
+    finally:
+        capture.release()
+    if total_frames <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"No frames decoded from video: {video_path!r}")
+    return total_frames
+
+
+def _load_video_frames_accvlab(
+    reader: Any,
+    video_path: str,
+    frame_indexes: Sequence[int],
+) -> Iterator[torch.Tensor]:
+    """Yield borrowed CUDA RGB frames, valid until the next reader decode."""
+    for frame_id in frame_indexes:
+        try:
+            decoded = reader.DecodeN12ToRGB([video_path], [frame_id], False)
+        except RuntimeError as exc:
+            # ACCV-Lab reports a request past the video's end with this error.
+            if str(exc) == "a frame after the last keyframe is currently not supported":
+                break
+            raise
+        yield torch.as_tensor(decoded[0])

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Numerical and storage-lifetime checks for GPU RGB Lanczos preprocessing."""
+
+import math
+import unittest
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+from PIL import Image
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mm.process.lanczos import resize_crop_normalize_rgb
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+def pillow_reference(array, height, width):
+    image = Image.fromarray(array)
+    scale = max(width / image.width, height / image.height)
+    resized = image.resize(
+        (math.ceil(scale * image.width), math.ceil(scale * image.height)),
+        Image.Resampling.LANCZOS,
+    )
+    left, top = (resized.width - width) // 2, (resized.height - height) // 2
+    cropped = resized.crop((left, top, left + width, top + height))
+    return (
+        torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(cropped, dtype=np.float32) / 127.5 - 1.0)
+        .permute(2, 0, 1)
+        .contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+class TestLanczosPreprocess(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_pillow_geometry_and_rounding(self):
+        rng = np.random.default_rng(9843)
+        shapes = [
+            ((704, 1280), (480, 832)),
+            ((480, 832), (704, 1280)),
+            ((101, 73), (64, 96)),
+            ((17, 31), (37, 21)),
+            ((32, 32), (32, 32)),
+            ((7, 9), (1, 1)),
+            ((1, 1), (24, 40)),
+            ((1, 43), (9, 17)),
+            ((43, 1), (17, 9)),
+            ((21, 17), (16, 16)),
+            ((73, 101), (55, 88)),
+            ((100, 101), (93, 93)),
+        ]
+        for source, target in shapes:
+            for pattern in ("random", "checkerboard", "impulse"):
+                with self.subTest(source=source, target=target, pattern=pattern):
+                    array = rng.integers(0, 256, (*source, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
+                    if pattern == "checkerboard":
+                        checkerboard = (
+                            (np.indices(source).sum(axis=0) % 2) * 255
+                        ).astype(np.uint8)
+                        array = np.repeat(checkerboard[..., None], 3, axis=2)
+                    elif pattern == "impulse":
+                        array[:] = 0
+                        array[source[0] // 2, source[1] // 2] = 255
+                    output = resize_crop_normalize_rgb(
+                        torch.from_numpy(array).cuda(), *target
+                    )
+                    expected = pillow_reference(array, *target)
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(output.cpu(), expected))
+                    self.assertEqual(output.dtype, torch.float32)
+                    self.assertTrue(output.is_contiguous())
+
+    def test_padded_rows_and_borrowed_input_lifetime(self):
+        rng = np.random.default_rng(72)
+        array = rng.integers(0, 256, (61, 93, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
+        storage = torch.empty((61, 110, 3), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+        borrowed = storage[:, :93]
+        borrowed.copy_(torch.from_numpy(array))
+        self.assertFalse(borrowed.is_contiguous())
+        output = resize_crop_normalize_rgb(borrowed, 40, 56)
+        # The output must own its pixels when a producer reuses its allocation.
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().synchronize()
+        borrowed.zero_()
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(output.cpu(), pillow_reference(array, 40, 56)))
+
+    def test_parameter_validation(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            resize_crop_normalize_rgb(torch.zeros((8, 8, 3), dtype=torch.uint8), 8, 8)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            resize_crop_normalize_rgb(
+                torch.zeros((8, 8, 4), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8), 8, 8
+            )
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            resize_crop_normalize_rgb(torch.zeros((8, 8, 3), device="cuda"), 8, 8)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            resize_crop_normalize_rgb(
+                torch.zeros((8, 8, 3), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8), 0, 8
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
